The Four Forces There are four forces associated with the flight of an airplane. These forces, illustrated in Figure 1.8, are lift, weight, thrust, and drag. In straight-and-level flight (not changing speed, direction, or altitude) the net lift on the airplane is equal to its weight. Mach Number One important parameter in describing high-speed flight is the Mach number. The Mach number is simply the speed of the airplane, or speed of the air, measured in units of the speed of sound. Thus, an air- plane traveling at a speed of Mach 2 is going twice the speed of sound. The speed of sound is fundamental for flight because it is the speed of communication between the airplane and the air, and between one part of the air and another.
